name: Suriname
summary: Under the new Civil Code (in force May 2025 according to a summary), the legitimate portion is abolished and a surviving spouse takes control of the estate, so children have no guaranteed share but only claims limited to money. Rules on foreign law, trusts and foundations could not be sourced.
family_claims: Children keep only a limited money claim once a testamentary right has been invoked; a cohabitant of at least 10 years may get a usufruct for maintenance over the home (per the Informea summary of Book 4). Details not read in the Code.
foreign_law_note: No source on Suriname's conflict-of-laws rule for succession or on a choice of foreign law was found.
trust_note: No trust law was found. Suriname is not a party to the Hague Trusts Convention. Foundations (stichtingen) exist in Dutch-derived law, but whether a private-benefit foundation is allowed was not sourced.
open_questions: The new Civil Code was read only via an Informea summary; verify the entry-into-force date, the abolition of the legitieme portie, and the transitional rules in the Staatsblad text.

Whether stichtingen can serve family-benefit purposes and whether any trust-like device exists was not sourced; domestic_trusts and private_foundations are 'no' because nothing was found, not because it is confirmed.
Conflict rules for succession were not found.
